data.name: Moto Racer Collection
data.detailed_description:
Moto Racer Collection features the original Moto Racer, Moto Racer 2, Moto Racer 3 Gold Edition + Moto Racer 15h Anniversary.

MOTO RACER / MOTO RACER 2: Retrace the series roots and tackle legendary races such as the famous Great Wall of China. Put your skills and reflexes to the test in Arcade and Simulation modes.

MOTO RACER 3: Feel the thrill of speeds 300 km/h and over on some of the world's greatest racetracks including Suzuka and the Sachsenring. Hop on a trial bike and negotiate the trickiest of obstacles. And take a nerveshredding high-speed trip through the streets of Paris.

MOTO RACER 15th ANNIVERSARY: Race against fierce competitors in GP Mode. Challenge the best bikers in spectacular Supercross races Perform the best aerial tricks in Freestyle Mode. Break the records in Time Trial Mode.

Key Features:


EVERY MOTORCYCLE CATEGORY UNDER THE SUN, BROUGHT TOGETHER IN ONE GAME

MOTO GP:
  • Hit speeds of over 300 km/h as you race flat out against the toughest of rivals.
SUPERCROSS:
  • Go head-to-head with your rivals in all-terrain races and tease them with your fanciest tricks.
FREESTYLE:
  • Pull off amazing Superman seat grabs, Indy backflips and can-cans as you fly through the air.
GAME PACKAGE INCLUDES:
  • Moto Racer, Moto Racer 2, Moto Racer 3 Gold Edition and Moto Racer 15th Anniversary

reviews.review:
Moto Racer Collection is a nostalgic motorcycle racing compilation that brings together four distinctive entries from a classic franchise, offering a combination of high-speed competition, off-road challenges, and stunt-based entertainment. Developed and published by Microids, the package includes Moto Racer, Moto Racer 2, Moto Racer 3 Gold Edition, and Moto Racer 15th Anniversary. Its greatest strength lies in preserving the straightforward excitement of traditional arcade racing, where responsive steering, quick reflexes, and precise cornering determine success. Rather than attempting to compete with sophisticated modern motorcycle simulators, the collection celebrates an accessible approach to racing that prioritizes entertainment and variety. Unfortunately, outdated technology and inconsistent compatibility prevent this otherwise appealing compilation from delivering a consistently satisfying experience.

The original Moto Racer provides an enjoyable introduction to the franchise's identity through fast-paced races across memorable environments. Courses inspired by locations such as the Great Wall of China add personality to the competition, while the combination of road and off-road motorcycles introduces different handling characteristics. The gameplay emphasizes maintaining momentum, anticipating corners, and finding opportunities to overtake opponents. Moto Racer 2 builds upon these foundations by offering Arcade and Simulation modes, allowing players to select between accessible handling and a more demanding racing experience. Although neither installment provides the realism expected from contemporary simulators, their uncomplicated mechanics retain an appealing sense of immediacy. However, their dated controls and limited technical refinement may frustrate newcomers unfamiliar with older racing games.

Moto Racer 3 Gold Edition expands the experience considerably by introducing additional motorcycle disciplines and more ambitious environments. High-speed competitions on recognizable circuits such as Suzuka and Sachsenring deliver exhilarating racing scenarios, with motorcycles capable of exceeding 300 kilometers per hour. The inclusion of trial riding creates a welcome alternative to conventional races, challenging players to negotiate difficult obstacles through careful control and precision. Racing through the streets of Paris adds another distinctive setting, emphasizing speed and environmental variety. These different activities demonstrate the franchise's willingness to experiment beyond traditional circuit racing. Nevertheless, the handling can feel inconsistent between disciplines, and certain gameplay elements lack the responsiveness and refinement necessary to make every challenge equally enjoyable.

Moto Racer 15th Anniversary provides another substantial selection of racing activities through its GP, Supercross, Freestyle, and Time Trial modes. GP competitions emphasize overtaking rivals and maintaining consistent racing lines, while Supercross introduces challenging terrain, jumps, and aggressive competition. Freestyle stands out by shifting attention toward spectacular aerial maneuvers, including Superman seat grabs, Indy backflips, and can-cans. These tricks introduce an entertaining alternative to conventional racing, rewarding experimentation and successful execution. Time Trial complements the experience by encouraging players to improve their personal records through repeated attempts. Although these activities provide considerable variety, their lasting appeal depends heavily on the player's enthusiasm for mastering relatively straightforward racing mechanics.

The compilation's visual presentation reflects its historical origins, featuring basic motorcycle models, simplified environments, and graphical effects that appear noticeably outdated by modern standards. Despite these limitations, several tracks possess recognizable characteristics that help distinguish one competition from another. The sensation of speed remains an important attraction, particularly during demanding road races where quick reactions are essential. Sound effects and motorcycle engines contribute to the racing atmosphere, although the overall audio quality lacks the detail and sophistication of newer productions. The presentation is therefore more likely to appeal to nostalgic enthusiasts than players seeking realistic visuals, advanced physics, or cinematic production values.

Multiplayer functionality provides another potential attraction, with the Steam listing advertising multiplayer, shared or split-screen gameplay, and Remote Play Together. These features offer opportunities for competitive entertainment beyond individual racing sessions, although actual functionality may vary between the included games. Unfortunately, technical reliability is a serious concern. The compilation depends on older software technologies, including DirectX 9 and legacy Microsoft components, which can create difficulties on contemporary Windows systems. Reported problems include launch failures, graphical glitches, missing audio, outdated display resolutions, and inconsistent controller support. Such issues are particularly disappointing because purchasing a collection should ideally provide convenient access to its included games without requiring extensive troubleshooting.

Steam Deck compatibility is officially classified as Unsupported, making this compilation an unsuitable recommendation for players expecting dependable handheld functionality. While unofficial compatibility adjustments may occasionally help individual titles operate, successful performance cannot be guaranteed. This limitation further highlights the absence of comprehensive modernization. The collection would benefit considerably from improved controller integration, updated graphical compatibility, streamlined configuration options, and technical fixes addressing its aging software dependencies. Without these improvements, players may spend more time resolving compatibility problems than enjoying the actual racing.

Ultimately, Moto Racer Collection offers an interesting opportunity to revisit a recognizable motorcycle racing franchise, but its appeal is substantially weakened by technical shortcomings. The diverse selection of racing disciplines, accessible arcade mechanics, memorable circuits, and freestyle activities provides genuine entertainment potential. However, the inconsistent functionality of its older installments makes the package difficult to recommend at full price. Its Mixed Steam reception reinforces the impression that nostalgic value alone cannot compensate for unreliable performance. Dedicated enthusiasts willing to experiment with compatibility fixes may still appreciate its historical significance, especially during a substantial discount. For newcomers seeking a polished and dependable motorcycle racing experience, better alternatives are available. 

Rating: 5/10
